method: Incremental review since 2026-09-24T06:24:02Z: refreshed metadata for all 57 selected reports (no issue-record changes); paginated new or edited comments on every selected report (none returned). Read the full bodies of #47836 and #38802, paginated the complete discussion of #47836 (no comments), and new or edited comments on #38802 (one returned). Separately rechecked metadata and paginated new or edited comments on #44739, #38663, #46207, and #46771 (none returned). Recorded the unspecified-platform voice-drag report and the broader Windows memory/stutter follow-up separately; no new Windows click/drag report was selected. Existing summaries, recovery classifications, and site copy remain accurate and unchanged. Counts describe this refresh; historical findings and exclusions remain unless qualified below. The public changelog was not rechecked in this incremental pass. Review dates and snapshot timestamps use UTC.

findings.finding: One explicit tracker duplicate connects the mouse-stall reports: #33840 is the duplicate and #33565 is canonical. Verified from the canonical and duplicate fields of the GitHub MarkedAsDuplicateEvent; the event is hosted on the canonical thread.

The input failures are not uniformly explained by multiple monitors or non-100% scaling. Some scale-sensitive variants improve at 100%; other reports reproduce on a single display at 100%. One commenter explicitly retracts a DPI-only inference.

Hover response is not proof of click delivery. Electron documents forwarding of mouse-move messages while other mouse events pass to the window underneath; reports include both working-hover and no-hover variants.

The proposed missing-native-input-region diagnosis is not established by a zero region-query return alone. Microsoft distinguishes an empty region from an absent region or API error. GetWindowRgn also requires a valid destination region handle. The reports’ failed hit-test samples remain observations; the claimed native cause remains an inference.

Community layered-window recoveries differ. Clearing and restoring the style helped one reproduction; another lost input again when the style was restored. A separate report describes recovery from setting layered-window alpha. These are local observations, not a universal workaround or a shipped product fix.

A linked external-proxy experiment moved the mascot visually but did not carry its live controls and activity surfaces with it. The linked PowerShell gist selects the first matching visible layered window by title/class, without verifying its owning process; it was read, not executed or adopted.

Closed/completed is not verified fixed: #41506 has later comments describing continued failure. Conversely, #39024 contains an explicit correction withdrawing its Codex-specific diagnosis after identifying a local Windows drag-outline setting.

Voice-overlay reports describe several different outcomes: an orb that focuses the app while its actions fail, a fully click-through orb, and a surface that blocks other applications. They are retained as adjacent comparisons, not diagnosed as one defect.

September 9 affected-user reports identify recoveries on Windows package 26.903.8094.0 and app version 26.903.61454. The counter-anchor follow-up describes working hover, clicks, and repeated drags without a workaround. These reports supersede the previous absence of an identified working build; they do not establish universal recovery or identify the implementing fix. Package and app version strings are retained as reported rather than treated as interchangeable.

#41513 was closed/completed on September 9. The closure is recorded separately from the preceding user recovery reports and does not make this thread an official master issue or establish that every related failure is fixed.

Failures are also reported with app version 26.905.11957 on Windows 10 and a Windows 11 multi-monitor setup. Release channels and package-to-app version mapping were not independently verified, so these are remaining reports, not proof that the reported working build universally regressed.

A first-hover report describes a local performance trace in which pet mouse events stop while animation timers and paint work continue. The raw trace is not attached; the report narrows the symptom but cannot distinguish the initiating native input defect.

Community experiments in #33224 and #42230 report input failure persisting with the input-shape branch disabled, directing attention to resize, opacity, and passthrough interactions beyond that branch alone. These are reported tests, not independently reproduced source-level diagnoses.

Temporary recovery still must be distinguished from a shipped fix. A layered reset restored dragging with lag and later recurrence; an alpha-based recovery was lost after reboot. The resize-helper author corrected an omitted passthrough step and reported that native scans could also miss a demonstrably working overlay.

September 9–10 follow-ups add recovery reports on #41465, #41501, #41960, and #42661. Three name version 26.903.8094.0; #41465 says latest update without a version. #42661 specifically reports working clicks and dragging after a full Windows reboot without the alpha workaround or repair helper. #41960 also verifies position persistence after restarting the app. These are affected-user observations, not a universal fix claim.

#41960 was closed/completed on September 10 after its recovery report. #41465, #41501, and #42661 remain open in this snapshot despite recovery language in their comments; comment intent does not override tracker state.

The same September 10 follow-up appears on #42945 and #43789: version 26.903.8094.0 accepts clicks and drags immediately after spawning, but the circular control below the pet reportedly becomes clipped. Count this as one cross-posted observation. The expected general cursor-following and reported hover animation are not treated as a verified animation defect; the comment does not establish that ordinary mouse tracking is intended. It also does not demonstrate renewed loss of input after release on this build.

A September 9 comment on #43200 reports that a layered-style toggle retained working input after restoring the original style across four displays, with the invisible blocking region absent during the test. This differs from the original report where restoring the style restored failure. It adds a workaround observation, without identifying a tested app version or establishing a product fix.

A later September 10 follow-up on #41535 reports recovery on Windows app version 26.903.61454, adding a specific version to that thread's recovery record. The comment does not describe test scope, and the ticket remains open at this snapshot.

A later September 10 commenter on #41465 reports continued click-through on package 26.831.2377.0, says the Microsoft Store offers no newer update, and reports only temporary relief from refreshing the pet. This is a remaining failure and user-reported update-availability limitation on an older package, not evidence that package 26.903.8094.0 regressed. Store availability was not independently checked.

A September 10 follow-up on #41784 reports undraggable built-in and custom pets after a full app restart. It supplies CLI component version 0.153.4 rather than a comparable desktop package version; the report cannot establish failure on the package identified in recovery reports.

#42927 was closed/completed on September 10. Its body still describes the original failure, and its only comment is the older automated potential-duplicate suggestion. No new recovery confirmation or tested working build is given in this thread, so this closure is recorded separately from confirmed recovery reports.

A later September 10 recovery report on #41535 identifies Windows package 26.903.9818.0, internal app 26.903.71938, and normal built-in-pet dragging after update/restart on the same dual-monitor setup. The commenter reports a change in the Windows hidden-overlay passthrough policy compared with 26.901.6511.0; this is a plausible implementation clue, not an independently reproduced causal diagnosis or an identified first fixed build.

A later September 10 comment on #43789 explicitly confirms dragging fixed. No subsequent contradiction was found in this review, so the still-open input report now receives a recovery dash. The comment supplies no version and does not establish that the separately reported clipped control recovered. The earlier duplicate post on #42945 remains partial recovery and does not inherit this comment.

A separate Windows report #44739 describes the pet briefly appearing then entering an AppRoutes error page with r is not a function on package 26.908.3777.0, while the main chat remains usable. A commenter reports the same avatar-overlay exception on macOS 26.908.31748. Bot suggestions and community comparisons do not establish a shared cause with other startup reports or the earlier click-through defect. This crash is linked separately from the input graph; recovery of input does not imply every later pet build is usable.

#37978 was closed/completed on September 12. Its body still describes the original 150%-versus-100% scaling behavior; its only comment is an older failure confirmation. There is no new recovery statement or identified fixed build in the thread. Record the tracker closure separately from verified recovery. No new or edited comments were returned for the 55 selected reports since the previous snapshot, so the six open-report recovery dashes are unchanged.

September 13 review: all 55 selected issue records are unchanged and no new or edited comments were returned since the previous snapshot. The graph remains at 47 open and eight closed reports, with six open-report recovery dashes. New Linux keyboard and Windows pet-sizing reports do not establish another Windows pointer-delivery failure.

On #44739, three September 12 comments report the separate avatar-overlay crash persisting on Windows package 26.908.4561.0; one also reports voice startup failing in the overlay. A later follow-up from that commenter reports recovery of the overlay and voice on Store package 26.908.4834.0 (internal app 26.908.40834), and says the reverse module import is absent in that package. No later contradiction was found. This is a version-specific community recovery report, not an independently reproduced fix or proof of universal recovery; #44739 remains open and outside the input-failure graph.

The current #44720 body describes a frontend module dependency cycle and isolated reproduction using the shipped macOS bundle; its experimental change removes the reverse import and reportedly eliminates the exception in five import/prefetch scenarios. The Windows bundle comparison on #44739 supplies additional cross-platform evidence for this separate renderer-crash family. Neither investigation was reproduced in this review, and the evidence does not connect the cycle to the earlier Windows click-through defect. A newer-package recovery on #44739 is recorded separately from #44720 tracker closure.

#43723 closed/completed after the reporter confirmed working voice-overlay clicks and dragging on the same Windows 10 machine following an update from package 26.901.6511.0 to 26.908.4834.0. The recovery record is retained, but the closed node receives no open-report dash. #42469 also closed/completed on September 15; its three older comments add no recovery or fixed-build confirmation. The six open-report recovery dashes remain unchanged.

Two new selected Windows reports describe remaining pet input trouble. #45253 combines mixed-monitor work-area placement with click-through and failed dragging but supplies no comparable version. #45575 documents click-through and an initial drag jump on older package 26.901.6511.0, with user-reported lack of an offered Store update. Neither establishes a regression in the newer package associated with recovery. Its automated link to #45253 is recorded as a reference; its suggested macOS match #45397 remains outside the graph.

A September 13 #43713 follow-up compares #43061 and #43200 but distinguishes successful initial hover followed by loss of input events while animation scheduling continues. The trace remains local and unreviewed here. The reporter explicitly leaves a shared stale-input/passthrough mechanism unproven; existing reference edges now include this community qualification.

The separate avatar-overlay crash #44739 is now closed, with another explicit Windows recovery confirmation on package 26.908.4834.0. Meanwhile #38663 has a September 14 report of brief startup mouse stuttering with Pet visible on that package, relieved by hiding Pet. Crash recovery and this broader performance symptom are recorded separately; neither establishes a new failure of pet click/drag delivery.

A September 19 follow-up on #33565 reports brief cursor stuttering specifically when a window-switch/minimize transition makes the main app active while the pet is visible. Switching to another foreground app does not reproduce it in the described comparison. Built-in and custom pets behave alike at 100% scaling; disabling minimize/maximize animations reportedly does not help. No tested app version or recovery is supplied. This narrows a community reproduction, not a verified native cause, GPU diagnosis, or connection to click-through.

New Windows pet reports remain distinct from the pointer-delivery graph: #46207 describes Pet Mini draft editing stopping after initial entry on package 26.911.7940.0 while Send remains usable; #46771 describes running-state animation returning to idle on app 26.915.31945. Both had no discussion at review. Their descriptions do not establish recurrence of the tracked click/drag defect; a claimed local animation patch is not a shipped recovery. All 57 selected issue states and the six open-report recovery dashes are unchanged.

A September 22 comment on the separate animation report #46771 reports the same symptom on macOS but supplies no app version, diagnostic evidence, or recovery. This broadens the community symptom report without establishing a shared cause or a Windows pointer-input regression. No selected issue state, summary, or recovery classification changes in this review.

New report #47836 describes voice-overlay jumping during drags toward ultrawide display edges and losing its chosen position after tab/window switching. It supplies neither a confirmed operating system nor app version and had no comments at review. Its links to Windows #42813 and Linux #45514 do not establish platform, a duplicate, or a shared cause, so it remains outside the Windows graph pending clarification.

A September 24 follow-up on #38802 reports excessive memory growth, system-wide mouse stuttering, and eventual crashes on Windows app 26.917.71314 with the mascot enabled. The commenter describes recurrence after showing the mascot again and says hiding it does not release already accumulated memory; restarting with it hidden restores normal usage. This is a user-reported symptom/workaround comparison, not a shipped recovery or verified root cause. It remains broader performance context, not evidence that the tracked pet click/drag defect returned.

limitations: GitHub search indexes may lag and wording/labels can omit relevant reports; this is a reviewed selection, not an exhaustive bug census.
Cross-posted observations, bot suggestions, and AI-assisted descriptions are not independent confirmations of a shared cause.
User-reported technical tests and community workarounds were not reproduced on this machine.
The complete broader macOS focus, Linux drag, and Windows performance families were not folded into the Windows pet input map.
privacy: Only review metadata, issue numbers, short editorial findings, and public source links are retained. Raw bodies, comments, profiles, native window/process/display identifiers, attachments, and diagnostics are not copied into the repository.
